groupFile  // Canonical SFM animation-group master
{
	// PROVENANCE
	// First generated on 2026-08-22 by the SFM Model Scanner knowledge builder
	// (tools/build_knowledge.py, repository chadchan3d/sfm-model-scanner, commit ca3ef2f).
	// That builder was retired on 2026-08-28 (commit 9e22c7b); its knowledge/*.tsv sources
	// are archived in that repository. Historical source hashes of that generation:
	// Knowledge SHA-256: 1d4dd8dd439f7a57907a09a482db30b196f5c831d101a84350322e776927cf57
	// Taxonomy SHA-256: f41d8e504459f20ce806e1ea0f918ac2cc7ed2d0a57f36c6acc7f7b46bb7178d
	// This file is now the authoritative Master. It is maintained only through controlled,
	// validated programmatic edits; its history is the Git history of
	// chadchan3d/sfm-character-tools. It is not regenerated from the archived sources.

	// DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
	//
	// This file is a universal compatibility map for Source Filmmaker animation
	// controls. Models use many inconsistent naming and rigging conventions for
	// equivalent functions; those conventions are gathered into a stable,
	// animator-facing semantic structure.
	//
	// The goal is not to impose a new naming standard on model creators. The goal is
	// to make different models feel familiar to animate despite differences in how
	// their controls were named or implemented.
	//
	// UNIFORMITY
	//
	// Uniformity means that the same practical function appears in the same semantic
	// place across models. It does not require models to share control names,
	// implementation types, rig structures, or authoring conventions.
	//
	// The universal Master handles conventions that can safely generalize by exact
	// name. Model-specific meaning that cannot safely generalize belongs to contextual
	// tooling rather than being forced into the global map.
	//
	// ANIMATOR WORKFLOW
	//
	// Animator usability is the governing rule.
	//
	// A useful taxonomy should let an animator predict where a control will be,
	// reach it with few unnecessary expansions, and see a list small enough to
	// understand without needing to know how the model creator built the rig.
	//
	// Organize controls according to how an animator would naturally look for and use
	// them while posing. Technical purity, implementation details, alphabetical order,
	// and maintainer convenience are secondary.
	//
	// SEMANTIC FUNCTION OVER IMPLEMENTATION
	//
	// Group controls primarily by what an animator would use them to manipulate, not
	// by whether they are bones, flexes, transforms, helpers, or another mechanism.
	// Different implementation types may therefore share the same semantic group.
	//
	// Implementation type remains useful evidence and may provide a soft internal
	// division, but it does not determine the animator-facing category.
	//
	// There is no universal rule that flexes should precede bones or that bones should
	// precede flexes. Primary and commonly useful controls should be easier to reach
	// than secondary, detailed, corrective, or helper controls. Implementation type
	// should act only as a tie-breaker when it genuinely improves readability.
	//
	// A bone is not inherently more useful than a flex, and a flex is not inherently
	// more useful than a bone. Judge the control by what it allows the animator to do.
	//
	// Naming is evidence, not proof. Model conventions are too inconsistent to infer
	// semantic purpose or implementation type safely from names alone.
	//
	// Established animator-facing convention may override a purely lexical reading of
	// a control name when real-model evidence consistently resolves that exact literal
	// to one canonical destination.
	//
	// TAXONOMY DEPTH
	//
	// Prefer the shallowest stable hierarchy that remains easy for an animator to
	// navigate.
	//
	// Avoid creating groups until a recurring functional domain becomes dense enough
	// that subdivision materially improves animator navigation. A subgroup must earn
	// the additional click by reducing search burden or making the controls easier to
	// understand.
	//
	// Do not subdivide merely because a technically narrower category can be invented.
	// Broad semantic categories are preferable while their real per-model contents
	// remain manageable.
	//
	// Category density should be judged primarily by the controls an animator actually
	// sees together on real models, not by the total number of aliases accumulated in
	// this universal file.
	//
	// Repeated subdivision has diminishing returns. The purpose of taxonomy is to make
	// controls easier to find, not to classify them as minutely as possible.
	//
	// CANONICAL DESTINATIONS
	//
	// The canonical destination set is defined by the Master taxonomy itself and by
	// its machine-readable taxonomy knowledge. This philosophy governs how controls
	// are assigned to those destinations; it does not define a separate competing
	// taxonomy.
	//
	// Collision, universality, and contextuality are therefore judged at the level of
	// the actual animator-facing Master destinations.
	//
	// FACIAL TAXONOMY
	//
	// Eyes contains the eye apparatus and direct eye-region actions: eyeballs, pupils,
	// gaze, blinking, eyelid positioning, widening, closing, squinting, eye creases,
	// and closely related direct eye controls.
	//
	// Upper Face contains brows, forehead, temples, and surrounding upper-face
	// expression tissue that is not more naturally part of the direct eye workflow.
	//
	// Mid Face contains cheeks, nose, nostrils, muzzle, and related central facial
	// anatomy.
	//
	// Lower Face contains mouth, lips, jaw, chin, corners, teeth, fangs, throat, and
	// related lower-face controls.
	//
	// Expressions contains named overall facial states, emotions, expression presets,
	// and other expression controls whose meaning is not more specifically established
	// as a local facial action.
	//
	// Explicit anatomy normally takes precedence over an emotional or expressive name.
	// Brows_Angry belongs with brows; EyeAngry belongs with eyes; Mouth_Frown belongs
	// with the lower face; generic Angry belongs under Expressions.
	//
	// Established convention may establish anatomical function even when the literal
	// does not name the anatomy explicitly. Smile, for example, belongs in Lower Face
	// when it is the conventional mouth-corner action, while Happy belongs under
	// Expressions when it represents an overall facial state.
	//
	// The governing distinction is practical animator-facing function: local facial
	// actions belong with the region they manipulate; overall expression states and
	// presets belong under Expressions.
	//
	// Tongue and Ears remain distinct when their controls represent meaningful,
	// recurring animator tasks of their own.
	//
	// BODY SHAPE
	//
	// Body Shape contains intended visible changes to anatomy, proportions, volume,
	// physical state, and other intrinsic body appearance controls.
	//
	// "Shape" describes the animator-facing result rather than the implementation.
	// Bones, flexes, and other control types may therefore all belong under Body Shape.
	//
	// Body Shape represents anatomy or appearance change as the intended result.
	// A control whose purpose is instead to repair or compensate for deformation
	// remains a Corrective even when that repair visibly changes anatomical volume.
	//
	// Body Shape should not be subdivided into increasingly minute anatomical groups
	// unless real per-model control density demonstrates that doing so materially
	// improves navigation.
	//
	// CLOTHING
	//
	// Clothing contains controls whose primary animator-facing purpose is manipulating,
	// fitting, opening, closing, hiding, exposing, shaping, or otherwise working with
	// garments and worn accessories.
	//
	// A clothing-related control should not be moved into a generic technical category
	// merely because its implementation is corrective or helper-like if the animator
	// would naturally look for it while working with that garment.
	//
	// CORRECTIVES
	//
	// Correctives contains controls whose primary purpose is to repair, compensate for,
	// or improve deformation, clipping, interaction, volume, geometry, or another
	// authored model/animation problem.
	//
	// Correctives are defined by purpose, not implementation type and not solely by
	// pose. A corrective may operate through a flex, bone, helper, or another control.
	//
	// Anatomical naming alone does not move a genuine corrective into an anatomical
	// group. A wrist, elbow, leg, mouth, or other body-part control whose primary
	// purpose is repairing pose or deformation remains a Corrective.
	//
	// Where a corrective exists specifically to operate, fit, hide, or accommodate an
	// animator-facing object such as clothing, hair, wings, or another clearly distinct
	// object domain, that object's category takes precedence when it better matches the
	// animator's actual workflow.
	//
	// In short:
	//
	//   intended anatomy or appearance change -> Body Shape
	//   ordinary anatomical posing             -> anatomical group
	//   pose/deformation repair                -> Correctives
	//   object-specific fit/repair              -> that object's group
	//
	// OBJECT-SPECIFIC PURPOSE TAKES PRECEDENCE
	//
	// Object-specific purpose takes precedence over generic corrective function.
	// A control that exists to fit, repair, hide, or accommodate a particular
	// animator-facing object belongs with that object. Clothing fit and
	// anti-clipping controls therefore belong in Clothing; hair fixes belong
	// in Hair; wing fixes belong in Wings.
	//
	// Use Correctives when a control repairs deformation or posing but has no
	// stronger object-specific semantic home. Implementation type does not
	// override practical animator use.
	//
	// For the same reason, vague technical categories such as Utilities and
	// Deformers are avoided. Their controls are placed according to what an
	// animator uses them to manipulate or accomplish; technical rig machinery
	// with no clearer semantic destination belongs in the appropriate Rig group.
	//
	// SELECTION WORKFLOW
	//
	// Anatomical and articulated groups should reflect how animators actually select
	// and pose structures.
	//
	// Recurring carpal/palm bones remain under Arms as secondary wrist/hand structure
	// so Fingers remains a clean digit-selection group.
	//
	// Similar workflow considerations apply to limb chains, toes, wings, tails,
	// articulated accessories, and other sequential structures. Spatial, anatomical,
	// side, hierarchy, or traversal order should be preserved when it is more useful
	// than alphabetical order.
	//
	// GENERIC AND MODEL-SPECIFIC NAMES
	//
	// Controls whose exact names contain too little globally stable semantic information
	// to classify safely across unrelated models remain Unknown in the universal Master.
	//
	// A control such as Bone.001 may be perfectly understandable on one particular
	// model while representing something entirely different on another. Local certainty
	// does not make a generic exact name universally safe.
	//
	// The universal Master should therefore prefer incomplete truth over convenient
	// false certainty.
	//
	// Model-local structural evidence may establish useful meaning for such controls,
	// but that belongs to model-specific organization rather than an unsafe global
	// exact-name assignment.
	//
	// BIPED AND OPAQUE BIP NAMES
	//
	// Association with a known rigging convention does not make every literal from
	// that convention semantically useful.
	//
	// Biped-derived names that explicitly identify stable anatomy or function may be
	// Universal when their exact animator-facing destination is invariant. However,
	// bare or opaque bip/Bip names and numbered variants may be used as generic bone
	// identifiers in Blender, converted models, and other authoring workflows, much
	// like Bone.001.
	//
	// Such names are not withheld because they look generic. They are withheld because
	// the literal itself may genuinely identify different structures on different
	// models. A bip-derived literal therefore requires independently stable semantic
	// information before receiving a Universal assignment.
	//
	// UBIQUITY RULE
	//
	// Judge literals by observed model usage, not by linguistic genericness.
	//
	// A control name may be short, ordinary, broad-looking, or meaningless outside
	// rigging culture while still functioning as a stable convention across real models.
	// Such names should not be withheld from Universal merely because they appear
	// generic in isolation.
	//
	// When an exact literal has strong, consistent real-world backing and its observed
	// meanings resolve to the same animator-facing Master destination, it belongs in
	// Universal. Evidence from the existing Master, convention corpora, and accumulated
	// real-world samples should be treated as evidence of actual model culture rather
	// than requiring the literal to be semantically self-explanatory.
	//
	// Frequency alone does not make a literal Universal, but established and consistent
	// usage does.
	//
	// Human-classified real-world samples are strong convention evidence. Silkworm's
	// accumulated classifications record how literals actually occur in released models
	// and should therefore carry particular weight when evaluating terse, generic-looking,
	// or otherwise lexically uninformative names.
	//
	// Silkworm is an accumulated, merged historical corpus. The number of literals or
	// members in a family may demonstrate the breadth and coherence of that naming
	// family, but must not be interpreted as independent-model frequency unless model
	// provenance actually establishes that fact.
	//
	// Silkworm's historical categories are evidence, not Master destinations. They must
	// be translated through this project's shallower animator-facing taxonomy before
	// their placements count as agreement for Universal classification.
	//
	// A standardized convention or toolchain does not need to arise independently in
	// multiple rig lineages to be Universal. Convention-specific origin is acceptable
	// when the exact literal's animator-facing destination is sufficiently invariant
	// across the models where that convention is used and no observed canonical
	// collision establishes otherwise.
	//
	// FAMILY-COHERENCE RULE
	//
	// A coherent naming family may provide semantic evidence for otherwise terse or
	// lexically uninformative members when the family's shared animator-facing function
	// is itself supported by real-model or convention evidence.
	//
	// Family size alone does not establish meaning or Universal status. A large opaque
	// numbered namespace may remain semantically empty, while a smaller but coherent
	// family surrounded by clearly related controls may strongly establish function.
	//
	// Family evidence therefore strengthens interpretation; it does not replace the
	// requirement that Universal exact names resolve safely to a canonical destination.
	//
	// CANONICAL-COLLISION COROLLARY
	//
	// Only exact-literal disagreement at the Master's canonical destination level
	// constitutes a Universal collision.
	//
	// Differences in technical rig role, hierarchy, implementation, terminology,
	// segmentation, capitalization, prefixes, suffixes, indexing schemes, translations,
	// or synonymous names do not create ambiguity when the relevant exact literal still
	// resolves consistently to the same animator-facing destination.
	//
	// A literal should be withheld from Universal when the same exact literal is
	// genuinely attested with meanings that require different Master destinations, or
	// when its correct destination depends on recognizable model-local context.
	//
	// Universal collisions are established from observed evidence, not merely from
	// conceivable alternative meanings. The fact that a literal could hypothetically
	// mean something else on some future model is not evidence against an otherwise
	// established Universal mapping.
	//
	// In short: generic-looking is not the same as ambiguous. Canonical ambiguity at
	// the Master level is what matters.
	//
	// This corollary concerns whether one exact literal carries consistent
	// meaning across model evidence. It does not license distributing one
	// native-Rebuild casefold family across different destinations; see
	// NATIVE-REBUILD CASEFOLD COMPATIBILITY.
	//
	// UNKNOWN, USELESS, AND IGNORE
	//
	// Unknown means that the universal Master cannot establish a safe semantic home
	// for the exact control name.
	//
	// Unknown may therefore contain both genuinely opaque controls and controls whose
	// purpose is understandable only in the context of a particular model.
	//
	// Useless contains controls that have been identified and audited but appear to
	// provide little practical animator value. They remain accessible as a safeguard
	// because unusual models or workflows may still make them useful.
	//
	// Unclear purpose is not evidence of uselessness. Assignment to Useless requires
	// positive audit evidence that the control provides little practical animator value.
	//
	// IGNORE is a stronger decision and should be used exceptionally. It is reserved
	// for controls known to be dead, generated, redundant, or otherwise devoid of
	// meaningful animator value such that hiding them is preferable to exposing them.
	//
	// Helper/support naming alone is never sufficient reason for Useless or IGNORE.
	// Helpers may provide useful fine posing, deformation correction, clipping
	// correction, attachment behavior, or control of unusual secondary structures.
	//
	// CLASSIFICATION AND ACCESSIBILITY
	//
	// Failure to establish a semantic classification is not, by itself,
	// justification for hiding a control. Uncertainty should remain accessible
	// unless positive evidence establishes that hiding is preferable.
	//
	// This clarifies the accessibility consequences of Unknown, Useless, and
	// IGNORE; it does not redefine them. Unknown means the universal semantic
	// destination cannot safely be established. Useless means the control has
	// been positively audited as providing little practical animator value,
	// yet remains accessible as a safeguard. IGNORE is an exceptional positive
	// determination that hiding is preferable to exposing the control.
	//
	// Mere uncertainty must never be sufficient reason for Useless or IGNORE.
	// Classification failure alone must not make an animator-facing control
	// inaccessible.
	//
	// ONE CONTROL, ONE UNIVERSAL ASSIGNMENT
	//
	// Preserve exact control spelling and case for compatibility.
	//
	// Each recognized exact control name receives only one universal assignment.
	//
	// If the same exact name is demonstrably used for different functions on unrelated
	// models and those functions require different canonical destinations, the static
	// Master must not pretend those meanings are compatible. Context-dependent
	// collisions belong to model-local tooling.
	//
	// Controls whose semantic purpose can be established with sufficient universal
	// confidence should be classified rather than unnecessarily left Unknown.
	// Verified implementation type may support that judgment but does not establish
	// semantic purpose by itself.
	//
	// NATIVE-REBUILD CASEFOLD COMPATIBILITY
	//
	// SFM's native Rebuild Control Groups compares control names using ASCII
	// case-insensitive identity: A-Z fold to a-z. Native Rebuild therefore treats
	// Hand_r, hand_r, and HAND_R as one identity, regardless of how many separate
	// exact spellings the Master records.
	//
	// Exact spelling and case must remain preserved as source/provenance
	// information. What the Master must additionally satisfy is destination
	// discipline: every group of exact spellings that collapse to the same
	// ASCII-folded identity must resolve to exactly one canonical full taxonomy
	// path. Case variants may coexist within that single destination; they must
	// never be distributed across different destinations.
	//
	// Canonical destination for such a family is chosen by the same animator-
	// facing, context-free semantics that govern the rest of this taxonomy, not
	// by which variant happens to carry which capitalization. Prefer the
	// clearest supported destination. Prefer a more specific destination only
	// when the evidence for that specificity is clear; when specificity is not
	// clearly supported, prefer the broader valid destination rather than
	// overclassifying.
	//
	// A runtime-only Rig* interpretation does not override an established
	// ordinary anatomical interpretation when the two share one native-Rebuild
	// identity. Rig groups remain correct for controls that are genuinely and
	// exclusively rig-specific; they are neither automatically preferred nor
	// automatically demoted merely because a family also touches an ordinary
	// anatomical group.
	//
	// When a family's members are attested in conflicting ordinary semantic
	// branches and available evidence does not establish a defensible common
	// destination, do not force a resolution. Leave it for deliberate human
	// review rather than guessing from capitalization or spelling alone.
	//
	// This is a required invariant of the Master, not a description of its
	// historical state. Older entries that predate this rule must be brought
	// into compliance; new entries must never violate it. It governs which
	// single path a family occupies and does not authorize deleting, renaming,
	// or otherwise altering any observed exact spelling.
	//
	// ORDERING PHILOSOPHY
	//
	// Semantic grouping comes first.
	//
	// Within a semantic group, animator workflow, usefulness, and family cohesion
	// determine the most useful ordering.
	//
	// Related variants should remain adjacent to their base control. Anatomical,
	// skeletal, articulated, sequential, and other spatial chains should retain
	// meaningful traversal order where that is more useful than alphabetization.
	//
	// Independent named controls may be alphabetized when doing so makes them faster
	// to locate. Alphabetical order is a navigation aid, not a maintenance rule.
	//
	// Implementation type may be used as a secondary internal organization where it
	// genuinely improves readability, but never at the cost of forcing the animator
	// to understand the model's implementation before finding a control.
	//
	// In short:
	//
	// 1. Semantic function.
	// 2. Animator workflow and practical usefulness.
	// 3. Family, anatomical, and spatial cohesion.
	// 4. Implementation type where useful.
	// 5. Alphabetical predictability where useful.
	//
	// Never reorganize controls merely for maintenance convenience.
	//
	// COVERAGE AND EVIDENCE
	//
	// Expand compatibility from real controls and real models rather than speculative
	// aliases.
	//
	// The universal Master is the zero-friction baseline for conventions that can
	// safely generalize across models. It should become increasingly comprehensive
	// without sacrificing universal correctness merely to reduce the Unknown group.
	//
	// Structural, contextual, or model-local evidence may support more complete
	// organization through companion tooling, but must not be used to smuggle
	// model-specific assumptions into this universal file.
	//
	// SFM-SURVIVAL RULE
	//
	// External rigging, DCC, game-engine, and model vocabularies are relevant to the
	// Master only insofar as their exact literals can survive into an SFM model.
	//
	// Direct occurrence in an SFM model or historical SFM corpus is the strongest
	// evidence that a literal survives the conversion pipeline. Documented
	// name-preserving export or conversion behavior may also establish survival even
	// when the exact literal has not yet been observed in the available SFM corpus.
	//
	// Upstream application terminology alone is not sufficient. UI labels, semantic
	// mapping slots, authoring-only controllers, generated handles, or other names that
	// are normally stripped, renamed, translated, or never exposed as model controls
	// should not enter Universal merely because they exist in the source application.
	//
	// The relevant question is therefore not simply whether Blender, Maya, Unreal,
	// MMD, 3ds Max, or another system uses a term, but whether that exact literal can
	// plausibly reach SFM intact and retain a stable animator-facing meaning there.
	//
	// SILKWORM-ABSENCE COROLLARY
	//
	// Absence from Silkworm is evidence, but not a veto.
	//
	// Because Silkworm is a large historical SFM corpus, failure to find an externally
	// documented literal there lowers confidence that the name commonly survives into
	// SFM. It does not prove that the literal cannot survive, that Silkworm never
	// encountered the relevant ecosystem, or that the semantic classification is wrong.
	//
	// The weight of Silkworm absence depends on the expected prevalence of the
	// convention in SFM, the historical corpus coverage available for that convention,
	// and whether the relevant export or conversion path normally preserves the name.
	//
	// Therefore:
	//
	//   observed in SFM/Silkworm
	//        -> strong direct survival evidence
	//
	//   not observed, but documented to survive name-preserving conversion
	//        -> valid candidate with weaker prevalence evidence
	//
	//   upstream terminology with no surviving model literal
	//        -> research evidence only
	//
	// Silkworm presence can strongly establish that an outside convention reached real
	// SFM models. Silkworm absence should reduce confidence proportionally, not erase
	// otherwise sound conversion evidence.
	//
	// MASTER / SCANNER CONTRACT
	//
	// The Master is the protected universal baseline. It contains exact control
	// names whose animator-facing semantic placement is safe without model-local
	// interpretation. When an exact control name is present in the Master, that
	// placement is authoritative for normal Organizer operation.
	//
	// The Scanner exists primarily to classify the remainder: controls the Master
	// cannot safely resolve by exact name. It may use Master-resolved controls as
	// semantic anchors and model context, but it must not automatically replace,
	// downgrade, or residualize a valid Master assignment.
	//
	// In particular:
	//
	//   Master canonical -> never automatically becomes Other X Controls
	//   Master canonical -> never automatically becomes Unknown
	//   Master canonical -> never automatically moves to another category
	//
	// The Scanner may still detect exceptionally strong model-local evidence that
	// conflicts with a Master assignment. Such disagreement is an audit signal,
	// not permission to rewrite the model's Master placement. Record it as a
	// MASTER_MAPPING_CONFLICT (or equivalent) for later review of the Master.
	//
	// A confirmed conflict may eventually show that an exact name should be
	// corrected, removed from the Master, or handled contextually. Changes to
	// universal knowledge require deliberate human review; Scanner inference never
	// promotes itself into the Master automatically.
	//
	// Scanner classifications are model-local. A classification learned for one
	// model, including an opaque or generic name such as Bone.001, must never
	// become a global exact-name mapping or influence an unrelated model merely
	// because the same literal appears there.
	//
	// Therefore the runtime relationship is:
	//
	//   Master resolves known exact names
	//        -> protected canonical placement
	//
	//   Scanner resolves remaining model-local controls
	//        -> canonical group, Other X Controls, or Unknown
	//
	//   strong Scanner disagreement with Master
	//        -> internal audit diagnostic only
	//
	// Uniformity comes from combining a stable universal baseline with contextual
	// interpretation where that baseline cannot safely reach, not from having the
	// Scanner repeatedly reinterpret controls that are already known.
	//
	// RIG-PRESENTATION PRESERVATION
	//
	// Universal taxonomy and rig-specific presentation are separate concerns.
	//
	// Contextual tooling may preserve useful presentation deliberately created
	// by an active rig when native SFM Rebuild would otherwise destroy that
	// presentation, provided doing so does not override an established Master
	// destination.
	//
	// The precedence is:
	//
	//   established Master semantic destination
	//        -> Master wins
	//
	//   no safe Master destination, but deliberate useful active-rig
	//   presentation exists
	//        -> contextual tooling may preserve that rig presentation
	//
	//   neither exists
	//        -> do not invent taxonomy or presentation merely to avoid
	//           uncertainty
	//
	// Rig-presentation preservation is contextual compatibility behavior, not
	// universal taxonomy. Specialized presentation should be preserved from
	// demonstrated rig behavior, not invented merely because a control becomes
	// hidden.
	//
	// Master owns semantic meaning; the active rig may own specialized
	// presentation where Master has no justified semantic destination. This is
	// consistent with the Master / Scanner contract above and the general
	// distinction between universal knowledge and model-local or contextual
	// tooling.
	//
	// NO TAXONOMY FOR COMPATIBILITY ALONE
	//
	// Do not add universal Master categories merely to preserve technical
	// structures belonging to particular rigs. Specialized rig mechanics or
	// presentation should be preserved contextually when justified, per
	// RIG-PRESENTATION PRESERVATION above, rather than causing expansion of
	// the universal taxonomy.
	//
	// A new Master category must still independently earn inclusion under
	// TAXONOMY DEPTH and ANIMATOR WORKFLOW above. It should represent a
	// recurring animator-facing semantic distinction whose subdivision
	// materially improves navigation or understanding.
	//
	// Compatibility problems alone are not sufficient justification for
	// generic technical catch-all categories such as Helpers, Utilities,
	// Deformers, or equivalent implementation-oriented buckets.
	//
	// This does not prohibit a semantic category merely because some of its
	// controls happen to be helpers. The distinction is that a category must
	// be justified by animator-facing purpose rather than by the need to
	// preserve a particular rig's technical presentation.
	//
	// CONTRIBUTIONS
	//
	// Found a model that breaks the Master? Submit it for review. Missing,
	// misclassified, conflicting, or newly encountered control names can be
	// incorporated into future versions so the Master improves model by model.
	//
	// Master:
	// https://chadchan3d.com/category/assets/#sfm-animation-groups-master
	//
	// Submit fixes/models in ChadChat, #3d-help:
	// https://chadchan3d.com/chat/

		"Eyes"
		{
			"groupColor"		"255 200 120 255"
			// ---- FLEX CONTROLS ----
			"control"		"left"
			"control"		"right"
			"control"		"Left PupilDown"
			"control"		"Right PupilDown"
			"control"		"Left PupilGrow"
			"control"		"Right PupilGrow"
			"control"		"Left PupilLeft"
			"control"		"Right PupilLeft"
			"control"		"Left PupilRight"
			"control"		"Right PupilRight"
			"control"		"Left PupilRound"
			"control"		"Right PupilRound"
			"control"		"Left PupilShrink"
			"control"		"Right PupilShrink"
			"control"		"Left PupilUp"
